title: A space is Hausdorff exactly when its diagonal is closed in the product

standard_prerequisites.name: The Hausdorff separation axiom and the product topology on the square, with the diagonal as the set of pairs with equal entries
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on Hausdorff spaces, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two conditions whose equivalence the statement asserts.

core_obligations: The forward direction: if X is Hausdorff and a pair is not on the diagonal, the proof takes disjoint open neighbourhoods of the two entries and observes that their product is an open neighbourhood of the pair contained in the complement of the diagonal, so the diagonal is closed (proof lines 349-353).

The converse: if the diagonal is closed and two points are distinct, the proof uses that the complement of the diagonal is open and therefore contains a basic open neighbourhood of the pair, which splits as a product of open sets whose second factors can be intersected to produce disjoint neighbourhoods of the two points (proof lines 353-361).
Conclusion: the two conditions are equivalent (proof line 361).
proof_roadmap: 正向：若 x ≠ y，取不交开邻域 U、V，则 U×V 是 (x,y) 的开邻域且与对角线不交，故对角线闭。
反向：对角线闭意味着其补开，取 (x,y) 处的基本开邻域 U×V，对两个因子做适当的交，得到 x 与 y 的不交开邻域。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the diagonal criterion for the Hausdorff property (author lemma at source lines 339-346, label lemma-Hausdorff). The proof (source lines 348-362) is a direct two-way argument whose converse direction carries the content: from the closedness of the diagonal the author takes a basic product neighbourhood of an off-diagonal pair and trims its two factors to obtain disjoint neighbourhoods of the two points (proof lines 353-361). The criterion is used later in the chapter when the Hausdorff property has to be checked on products. H2.
